Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite alphabets, let $p$ be a pmf on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. A test channel is a stochastic matrix $W(\hat x\mid x)$, and its expected single-letter distortion is $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)$, with block distortion as in [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]. Put $D_{\min}=\sum_xp(x)\min_{\hat x}d(x,\hat x)$. Define, in bits,
$$
R_{p,d}(D):=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\min_{W:\,\mathbb E d(X,\hat X)\le D} I(X;\hat X),&D\ge D_{\min},\\[4pt]+\infty,&D<D_{\min}. \end{cases}
$$
The minimum exists by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]. Values are not operational code rates; the finite memoryless coding theorem is a separate claim.

Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite sets, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. Put
$$
D_{\min}:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p(x)\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}d(x,\hat x).
$$
For every $D\ge0$, the feasible stochastic channels $W(\hat x\mid x)$ satisfying $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)\le D$ form a nonempty set exactly when $D\ge D_{\min}$. Whenever nonempty, mutual information in bits attains its minimum over this set.

Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and $(\widehat{\mathcal X},\widehat{\mathcal A})$ be measurable spaces, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,+\infty]$ be a measurable single-letter distortion. For a positive integer $n$ and ordered blocks $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathcal X^n$ and $\widehat x^n=(\widehat x_1,\ldots,\widehat x_n)\in\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$, define the normalized additive block distortion by

$$d_n(x^n,\widehat x^n):=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^{n}d(x_t,\widehat x_t).$$

If the same ordered blocks are labeled $x_a^{a+n-1}:=(x_a,\ldots,x_{a+n-1})$ and $\widehat x_a^{a+n-1}:=(\widehat x_a,\ldots,\widehat x_{a+n-1})$, for any integer $a$, the equivalent formula is

$$d_n(x_a^{a+n-1},\widehat x_a^{a+n-1})=\frac1n\sum_{i=a}^{a+n-1}d(x_i,\widehat x_i).$$

The substitution $i=a+t-1$ gives the defining sum, so changing the coordinate labels changes neither the block distortion nor its normalization. In particular, blocks $X_0^{n-1}$ use the indices $0,\ldots,n-1$, while blocks $X^n=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ use $1,\ldots,n$.

When the alphabets are finite and nonempty and $d$ is finite-valued, define $d_{\max}:=\max_{x,\widehat x}d(x,\widehat x)$. Expected distortion is $\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)$; the excess-distortion probability at threshold $D$ is $\mathbb P(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D)$. These are distinct criteria: one is an expectation and the other is a tail probability.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

For finite $X,Y,Z$,

$$I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)\ge0.$$

Equality holds if and only if, for every $z$ with $p_Z(z)>0$, the conditional joint pmf factors as $p_{XY|z}=p_{X|z}p_{Y|z}$; this is conditional independence given $Z$.

For any $b>1$, define each base-$b$ finite information quantity by replacing $\ln$ with $\log_b$ in its defining finite formula. Then

$$H_b(p)=\frac{H(p)}{\ln b},\qquad D_b(p\|q)=\frac{D(p\|q)}{\ln b},$$

where the second equality is in $[0,+\infty]$ and $+\infty/\ln b:=+\infty$. The same conversion holds for finite conditional entropy, mutual information, and conditional mutual information. In particular, values in bits equal nats divided by $\ln2$.

derivations.claim: Uniform time-sharing produces a finite test channel with source marginal P_S and expected distortion D_k.
The IID mutual-information chain rule and nonnegative conditional mutual information show I(S^k;S-hat^k) >= sum_i I(S_i;S-hat_i).

Time-sharing and nonnegative conditional mutual information bound the single-letter mutual information by the block value; feasibility and base conversion give ln(2)R(D_k) <= k^{-1}I_nats(S^k;S-hat^k).

Let $\mathcal S,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\widehat{\mathcal S}$ be nonempty finite alphabets, let $P_S$ be a probability vector on $\mathcal S$, and let $W$ be a finite discrete memoryless channel from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ as in [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]]. For positive integers $k,n$, a deterministic **$(k,n)$ joint source-channel code** is a pair of maps
$$f_k:\mathcal S^k\to\mathcal X^n,\qquad g_k:\mathcal Y^n\to\widehat{\mathcal S}^{\,k}.$$
The source block has law $P_S^{\otimes k}$, the channel output conditional on input $x^n$ has law $W^n(\cdot\mid x^n)$, and the reproduction is $\widehat S^k=g_k(Y^n)$. The code has no feedback.

A **code sequence at channel-use ratio $\rho$** consists of such codes with source lengths $k\to\infty$, channel lengths $n_k$, and $n_k/k\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$. In the lossless case $\widehat{\mathcal S}=\mathcal S$, its block error is $\Pr[\widehat S^k\ne S^k]$. In the lossy case, for finite nonnegative single-letter distortion $d$, its normalized block distortion is $d_k$ from [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]; expected distortion and the positive-slack excess-distortion probabilities $\Pr[d_k>D+\varepsilon]$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ are distinct criteria.

For an input probability vector $P_X$ on $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]), let $P_{XY}(x,y):=P_X(x)W(y\mid x)$ and $Q_{P_X}(y):=\sum_xP_X(x)W(y\mid x)$. Write $I(P_X;W):=I(X;Y)$ for this joint law, using [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]. The **single-letter information capacity** is
$$C(W):=\sup_{P_X} I(P_X;W),$$
measured in nats per channel use. The finite-dimensional maximum is attained, as proved in [[lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity-is-attained]].

A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable** for $W$ if there are length-$n$ codes for all sufficiently large $n$ with
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\ln M_n}{n}\ge R,\qquad \varepsilon_{\rm av}(n)\longrightarrow0.$$
It is **maximal-error achievable** if the same condition holds with $\varepsilon_{\max}(n)\to0$. Define $C_{\rm av}(W)$ and $C_{\max}(W)$ as the suprema of the respective achievable-rate sets. Rates use nats per channel use.

For every finite DMC $W$ with no input-cost constraint,
$$C_{\rm av}(W)=C_{\max}(W)=C(W)=\max_{P_X}I(P_X;W),$$
with rates and mutual information measured in nats per channel use.

Let $P_S$ be a probability vector on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal S$, and define its entropy in nats by

$$H(P_S):=-\sum_{s:P_S(s)>0}P_S(s)\ln P_S(s).$$

For every $R>H(P_S)$, there are deterministic fixed-length codes $f_k:\mathcal S^k\to[M_k]$, $g_k:[M_k]\to\mathcal S^k$ for the IID source $P_S^{\otimes k}$ such that $\Pr[g_k(f_k(S^k))\ne S^k]\to0$ and $\limsup_{k\to\infty}k^{-1}\ln M_k<R$.
For every input probability vector on $\mathcal X^n$ and output $Y^n$ generated by a finite DMC $W^n$, one has $I(X^n;Y^n)\le nC(W)$.

Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

with equality if and only if $I(X;Y|Z)=0$, equivalently $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given every positive-mass value of $Z$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

derivations.claim: If $H(P_S)=0$, each nonzero term $-P_S(s)\ln P_S(s)$ is nonnegative, so exactly one source letter has probability one. Choose that letter $s_0$ and any channel input letter $x_0$, encode every source block as $x_0^{n_k}$, and decode every output to $s_0^k$. This is a deterministic joint code with zero error.

Now assume $0<H(P_S)<\rho C(W)$. Choose $\eta>0$ with $H(P_S)+2\eta<\rho C(W)$. By [F4], choose source codes with message counts $M_k$, source block error tending to zero, and $\limsup_k k^{-1}\ln M_k\le H(P_S)+\eta$. Then $\limsup_k n_k^{-1}\ln M_k\le(H(P_S)+\eta)/\rho<C(W)$.

For any joint code, $\widehat S^k$ is a function of $Y^{n_k}$, so [F7] gives $I(S^k;\widehat S^k)\le I(S^k;Y^{n_k})$. The encoder is deterministic and the DMC output law given $S^k=s^k$ is $W^{n_k}(\cdot\mid f_k(s^k))$; averaging its finite conditional entropies by the value of $X^{n_k}=f_k(S^k)$ gives $H(Y^{n_k}\mid S^k)=H(Y^{n_k}\mid X^{n_k})$. By [F8], $I(S^k;Y^{n_k})=I(X^{n_k};Y^{n_k})$, which is at most $n_kC(W)$ by [F2] and [F5]. If $p_k=\Pr[\widehat S^k\ne S^k]$, then [F6] and [F8] give $kH(P_S)\le n_kC(W)+\ln2+p_k k\ln|\mathcal S|$. Dividing by $k$ and taking $k\to\infty$ along a reliable code sequence proves $H(P_S)\le\rho C(W)$.

Choose a rate $R_c$ strictly between $(H(P_S)+\eta)/\rho$ and $C(W)$. By [F3] and the supremum property, some maximal-error achievable rate $R'>R_c$ exists, so its channel-code sequence has $\liminf_n n^{-1}\ln L_n\ge R'$ and maximal errors tending to zero. Since $n_k\to\infty$, eventually $\ln L_{n_k}/n_k>R_c>\ln M_k/n_k$. Restrict each such code to $M_k$ messages; mapping any discarded decoder output to a retained message preserves every retained message's former correct-decoding event, so maximal error does not increase.

Compose the source encoder and decoder from step 1.2 with the restricted channel code from step 2.1. The source-code index can have any distribution, but its channel decoding error is at most the maximal error. The joint block-error event is contained in the union of the source-code error event and the channel message-error event, so its probability is at most the sum of those two probabilities and tends to zero.

Step 1.1 gives zero-error achievability when the source entropy is zero; steps 1.2, 2.1, and 3.1 give reliable achievability under the strict positive-entropy threshold; and step 1.3 gives the necessary condition. Thus the stated strict-threshold conclusions hold, with no claim at the positive-entropy equality boundary.

boundaries.reason: Finite nonempty source and DMC alphabets provide fixed letters for the zero-entropy construction.

reviewed.reason: Statement and complete Proof: the entropy sum is over the positive support of the probability vector P_S, which is nonempty because its mass is one. All block entropy sums likewise concern normalized finite laws, and k,n_k are positive. The H=0 branch in step 1.1 chooses the unique mass-one source letter and an input letter of the explicitly nonempty DMC; it does not select from an empty set. The generic sum detector therefore exposes no admitted empty index family in this theorem.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1: The H=0 source is handled separately by a zero-error constant code.
Step 1.1: Singleton source alphabets are included in the H=0 branch; all k,n_k are positive.
Step 1.1: Zero channel capacity is covered when H=0; for H>0 it cannot satisfy the strict achievability condition.
Step 1.1: Strict H<rho C gives achievability and H>rho C is impossible; positive-entropy equality is not claimed.
Step 1.1: All codebooks, message sets, and source alphabets are finite; no arbitrary choice axiom is used.

risk_review.notes: Read all six current proof steps and all ten direct suppliers. H=0 implies singleton positive support and a constant zero-error reproduction, even at C=0. For H>0 the strict margin gives source rate < rho*C and a maximal-error achievable channel rate strictly above the normalized message count; n_k/k -> rho>0 gives n_k -> infinity, and restricting codes preserves correct events. Maximal error controls the nonuniform source index. Deterministic encoding gives equal conditional output entropies; DPI, the arbitrary-input n-letter bound, chain rule and Fano give kH <= n_k*C+ln(2)+p_k*k*ln|S|. Division proves the necessary weak inequality. Checked singleton alphabets, source zero masses, zero-capacity channels, arbitrary prescribed n_k and the deliberately unasserted positive-entropy equality case. Reader/refuter have no finding. No repair needed.

Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and $(\widehat{\mathcal X},\widehat{\mathcal A})$ be measurable spaces, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,+\infty]$ be a measurable single-letter distortion. For a positive integer $n$ and ordered blocks $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathcal X^n$ and $\widehat x^n=(\widehat x_1,\ldots,\widehat x_n)\in\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$, define the normalized additive block distortion by

$$d_n(x^n,\widehat x^n):=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^{n}d(x_t,\widehat x_t).$$

If the same ordered blocks are labeled $x_a^{a+n-1}:=(x_a,\ldots,x_{a+n-1})$ and $\widehat x_a^{a+n-1}:=(\widehat x_a,\ldots,\widehat x_{a+n-1})$, for any integer $a$, the equivalent formula is

$$d_n(x_a^{a+n-1},\widehat x_a^{a+n-1})=\frac1n\sum_{i=a}^{a+n-1}d(x_i,\widehat x_i).$$

The substitution $i=a+t-1$ gives the defining sum, so changing the coordinate labels changes neither the block distortion nor its normalization. In particular, blocks $X_0^{n-1}$ use the indices $0,\ldots,n-1$, while blocks $X^n=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ use $1,\ldots,n$.

When the alphabets are finite and nonempty and $d$ is finite-valued, define $d_{\max}:=\max_{x,\widehat x}d(x,\widehat x)$. Expected distortion is $\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)$; the excess-distortion probability at threshold $D$ is $\mathbb P(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D)$. These are distinct criteria: one is an expectation and the other is a tail probability.

Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite alphabets, let $p$ be a pmf on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. A test channel is a stochastic matrix $W(\hat x\mid x)$, and its expected single-letter distortion is $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)$, with block distortion as in [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]. Put $D_{\min}=\sum_xp(x)\min_{\hat x}d(x,\hat x)$. Define, in bits,
$$
R_{p,d}(D):=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\min_{W:\,\mathbb E d(X,\hat X)\le D} I(X;\hat X),&D\ge D_{\min},\\[4pt]+\infty,&D<D_{\min}. \end{cases}
$$
The minimum exists by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]. Values are not operational code rates; the finite memoryless coding theorem is a separate claim.

Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite sets, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. Put
$$
D_{\min}:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p(x)\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}d(x,\hat x).
$$
For every $D\ge0$, the feasible stochastic channels $W(\hat x\mid x)$ satisfying $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)\le D$ form a nonempty set exactly when $D\ge D_{\min}$. Whenever nonempty, mutual information in bits attains its minimum over this set.

Let $X_0,X_1,\ldots$ be a source over a finite alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite, and let $d$ be finite-valued. An $n$-block fixed-length code with $M_n$ messages is a deterministic encoder $f_n:\mathcal X^n\to[M_n]$ and decoder $g_n:[M_n]\to\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$; its reconstruction is $\widehat X^n=g_n(f_n(X^n))$, its block distortion is [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]], and its rate is $n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ bits per source symbol.

Define the expected-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{avg}}(D)$ as the infimum of $\limsup_n n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ over code sequences satisfying $\limsup_n\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\le D$. Define the positive-slack excess-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{slack}}(D)$ by the same rate infimum over code sequences satisfying

$$\text{for every }\varepsilon>0,\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D+\varepsilon\right)\longrightarrow0.$$

The expected and positive-slack excess criteria are separate definitions. An exact-threshold condition $\mathbb P(d_n>D)\to0$ is not part of either definition.

Let $(X_i)_{i\ge0}$ be iid with a pmf on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be finite nonnegative distortion. For every $D\ge0$, the expected-distortion and positive-slack excess-distortion operational rates of [[def-it-operational-rate-distortion-function]] both equal the finite information rate-distortion function of [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]], with value $+\infty$ when $D<D_{\min}$.

A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable** for $W$ if there are length-$n$ codes for all sufficiently large $n$ with
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\ln M_n}{n}\ge R,\qquad \varepsilon_{\rm av}(n)\longrightarrow0.$$
It is **maximal-error achievable** if the same condition holds with $\varepsilon_{\max}(n)\to0$. Define $C_{\rm av}(W)$ and $C_{\max}(W)$ as the suprema of the respective achievable-rate sets. Rates use nats per channel use.

For a finite DMC $W$, a **length-$n$ code with $M$ messages** is a pair of maps $e:[M]\to\mathcal X^n$ and $d:\mathcal Y^n\to[M]$, where $n,M\ge1$ and $[M]:=\{1,\ldots,M\}$. A message $m$ is encoded as $e(m)$, passed through the block kernel $W^n$ of [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]], and decoded as $d(Y^n)$. The encoder and decoder are deterministic; there is no feedback, and no input-cost constraint is imposed.

For a length-$n$ code $(e,d)$, let
$$e_m:=W^n\{y^n:d(y^n)\ne m\mid e(m)\}.$$
Its **average error** is $\varepsilon_{\rm av}:=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M e_m$, corresponding to a uniform message, and its **maximal error** is $\varepsilon_{\max}:=\max_{1\le m\le M}e_m$.

For every finite DMC $W$ with no input-cost constraint,
$$C_{\rm av}(W)=C_{\max}(W)=C(W)=\max_{P_X}I(P_X;W),$$
with rates and mutual information measured in nats per channel use.

Let $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ be IID with law $P_S$ on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal S$, let $\widehat{\mathcal S}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal S\times\widehat{\mathcal S}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. For any joint law of $S^k$ and $\widehat S^k$, put $D_k:=\mathbb E d_k(S^k,\widehat S^k)$, using the normalized block distortion of [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]. If $R(D)$ is the finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function in bits from [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]], then

$$\ln2\,R(D_k)\le\frac1k I(S^k;\widehat S^k),$$

where mutual information on the right is in nats. The test channel induced by the joint law is feasible at distortion $D_k$, so the rate-distortion minimum is attained there by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]].

Let the source and reproduction alphabets be finite nonempty sets and let the distortion be finite-valued and nonnegative. The finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function $R(D)$ of [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]] is finite and nonincreasing on $[D_{\min},\infty)$, convex there, zero for $D\ge D_{\rm c}:=\min_{\hat x}\mathbb E d(X,\hat x)$, and right-continuous at every feasible distortion, including $D_{\min}$.
For every input probability vector on $\mathcal X^n$ and output $Y^n$ generated by a finite DMC $W^n$, one has $I(X^n;Y^n)\le nC(W)$.

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

derivations.claim: Suppose $R(D)=0$. By [F1] choose a minimizing test channel; its mutual information is zero in bits and hence in nats by [F9]. This finite weighted average implies some $\hat s_0$ has $\mathbb E d(S,\hat s_0)\le D$. Use one message, a fixed channel input word, and the constant reproduction $\hat s_0^k$. Its expected distortion is at most $D$. For each $\varepsilon>0$, the IID bounded variables $Z_i=d(S_i,\hat s_0)$ have mean at most $D$, finite variance, and variance of their average equal to $\operatorname{Var}(Z_1)/k$; the pointwise bound $\mathbf1_{\{|\overline Z-\mathbb EZ_1|\ge\varepsilon\}}\le(\overline Z-\mathbb EZ_1)^2/\varepsilon^2$ gives $\Pr[k^{-1}\sum_iZ_i>D+\varepsilon]\le\operatorname{Var}(Z_1)/(k\varepsilon^2)\to0$.

Now assume $R(D)>0$ and $r(D)<\rho C(W)$. Choose $R_c$ with $r(D)/\rho<R_c<C(W)$, then choose $\eta>0$ so that $(\ln2)(R(D)+\eta)/\rho<R_c$. For either chosen source performance criterion, [F2] gives deterministic source codes with message counts $M_k$, that criterion, and $\limsup_k k^{-1}\log_2M_k\le R(D)+\eta$. Therefore $\limsup_k n_k^{-1}\ln M_k\le(\ln2)(R(D)+\eta)/\rho<R_c$.

For any joint code, [F7] gives $I(S^k;\widehat S^k)\le I(S^k;Y^{n_k})$. Given $S^k=s^k$, the DMC output has law $W^{n_k}(\cdot\mid f_k(s^k))$; averaging conditional entropies over source words and grouping them by $X^{n_k}=f_k(S^k)$ gives $H(Y^{n_k}\mid S^k)=H(Y^{n_k}\mid X^{n_k})$. Therefore [F10] yields $I(S^k;Y^{n_k})=I(X^{n_k};Y^{n_k})$, and [F6] bounds this by $n_kC(W)$. The rate-distortion bound [F4] at the actual expected distortion $D_k=\mathbb E d_k$ then gives $r(D_k)\le(n_k/k)C(W)$.

Since $R_c<C(W)$, [F3] and the supremum definition of maximal-error capacity give a maximal-error achievable rate strictly greater than $R_c$. Its channel code sequence has enough messages to include $M_k$ for all sufficiently large $n_k$; restrict to those messages, mapping discarded decoder outputs to a retained message. Correct-decoding regions for retained messages are preserved, so maximal error does not increase. The source-code index may be nonuniform, but its channel error is the weighted average of per-message errors and is bounded by the maximal error.

If the expected-distortion criterion holds, then for every $\varepsilon>0$, eventually $D_k\le D+\varepsilon$. Monotonicity in [F5] and step 1.3 imply $r(D+\varepsilon)\le(n_k/k)C(W)$; taking $k\to\infty$, then $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and using right-continuity in [F5] yields $r(D)\le\rho C(W)$.

Compose the source and channel codes. On channel success the reproduction equals the source-code reproduction, while on channel error the normalized distortion is at most $d_{\max}$. A **finite discrete memoryless channel (DMC)** is the channel sequence [[def-channel-sequence]] with fixed finite nonempty input and output alphabets $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ (with every subset measurable) and one stochastic kernel $W(y\mid x)$ from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ ([[def-finite-stochastic-kernel]]). At every blocklength its input and output alphabets are $\mathcal X^n,\mathcal Y^n$, and its block kernel is
$$W^n(y^n\mid x^n):=\prod_{i=1}^n W(y_i\mid x_i).$$
Thus the same single-use transition law is applied independently at each coordinate, conditional on the input word. This page imposes no feedback or input-cost constraint.

For an input probability vector $P_X$ on $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]), let $P_{XY}(x,y):=P_X(x)W(y\mid x)$ and $Q_{P_X}(y):=\sum_xP_X(x)W(y\mid x)$. Write $I(P_X;W):=I(X;Y)$ for this joint law, using [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]. The **single-letter information capacity** is
$$C(W):=\sup_{P_X} I(P_X;W),$$
measured in nats per channel use. The finite-dimensional maximum is attained, as proved in [[lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity-is-attained]].

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$. It is the weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Write $p_Y(y)=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. For each $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$, set $p_{X|y}(x)=p_{XY}(x,y)/p_Y(y)$; this is a probability vector by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. Define the conditional entropy in nats by

$$H(X|Y):=\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(p_{X|y}),$$

where $H(p)=-\sum_xp(x)\ln p(x)$ is the finite entropy of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. Terms for zero-mass $y$ are omitted. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.
For finite probability vectors $p,q$ on the same alphabet, $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$. If $p_i>0=q_i$ for some coordinate, then $D(p\|q)=+\infty$.

For every finite DMC $W$ with no input-cost constraint,
$$C_{\rm av}(W)=C_{\max}(W)=C(W)=\max_{P_X}I(P_X;W),$$
with rates and mutual information measured in nats per channel use.

Let $S_1,S_2,\ldots$ be IID with probability vector $P_S$ on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal S$, and let $W$ be a finite DMC with capacity $C(W)$ in nats per channel use. Write $H(P_S):=-\sum_{s:P_S(s)>0}P_S(s)\ln P_S(s)$ for source entropy in nats. Fix positive integers $n_k$ with $n_k/k\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$. A deterministic $(k,n_k)$ joint code is as in [[def-it-point-to-point-joint-source-channel-code]]. If $H(P_S)=0$, a zero-error code sequence exists for every such $W$. If $H(P_S)<\rho C(W)$, there are codes with block error tending to zero. Conversely, every code sequence with block error tending to zero satisfies $H(P_S)\le\rho C(W)$. Thus strict violation $H(P_S)>\rho C(W)$ rules out reliable transmission; the positive-entropy equality boundary is not asserted.
